addon.name: Hisense TV remote: blue button to ContextMenu

extension.summary: Remaps a Hisense TV remote's blue button (received over HDMI-CEC) to Kodi's ContextMenu
extension.description: Run this once from Program add-ons. Installs userdata/keymaps/custom_remote.xml, remapping the blue button on a Hisense TV remote from Kodi's default ActivateWindow(Pictures) to ContextMenu - the TV's own dedicated Menu button doesn't pass through CEC at all on this hardware (confirmed with cec-client -m: no User Control Pressed event ever reaches CoreELEC for it), while the coloured buttons do. Blue was picked since Pictures isn't otherwise used on this box; useful for addons like this repo's CU LRC Lyrics fork, whose sync/reload/delete options live in a context menu. This is a GLOBAL keymap change, not specific to any one addon. If custom_remote.xml already exists with different content, asks before overwriting rather than silently replacing what looks like an unrelated existing customization. Requires a Kodi restart to take effect. Only tested on a Hisense TV over CEC on CoreELEC (x96max) - check with cec-client -m first on other hardware to confirm the blue button (or whichever you remap) actually reaches CoreELEC before relying on this.
extension.news: 1.3.0: now also runs a one-time check at Kodi boot (added the xbmc.service extension point, same as script.cu.lrclyrics.advanced's own font auto-install) instead of only ever running when the user manually opens it from Program add-ons - confirmed live that installing this addon alone does nothing until it's actually run, which nobody would know to do without reading the README first. Offers the same install confirmation automatically once per box, and if accepted, immediately offers to restart Kodi right then instead of just telling the user to do it themselves later. Only ever asks once, even on "no" - the manual settings actions are unaffected and always run when triggered. 1.2.0: replaced whole-file backup/restore with structural XML merge/strip - install now adds this addon's blue-to-ContextMenu remap into an existing custom_remote.xml section by section (via ElementTree) instead of overwriting or backing up the whole file, and remove() strips out exactly the <blue>ContextMenu</blue> entries this addon's own sections added, leaving anything else in the file (the user's own sections, other button remaps, even edits made after this addon's own install) completely untouched. Handles a file that was: never touched, had unrelated content before install, or was further edited afterward - the old file-level backup approach couldn't tell these apart correctly. Only ever touches a <blue> entry whose value is still exactly "ContextMenu" - a deliberate later change by the user to something else is left alone. 1.1.0: added a settings screen with explicit Install and "Restore original keymap" actions - Kodi has no uninstall hook for script add-ons (clicking Uninstall in the add-on browser just deletes this add-on's files, it never runs any of our code), so reverting the keymap change can only ever be this separate, explicit action, run BEFORE uninstalling. Install now also backs up an existing different custom_remote.xml before overwriting it, so Restore can bring it back. 1.0.0: initial release - packages the Hisense blue-button-to-ContextMenu keymap fix (previously a manual-copy-only file under keymaps/hisense-blue-contextmenu/) as a proper installable addon.

addon.name: CoreELEC: Network watchdog (connman restart on boot)

extension.summary: Restarts connman on a loop until a real LAN IP shows up at boot
extension.description: Run this once from Program add-ons. Installs a systemd oneshot service (network-watchdog.service) and its script to /storage/.config/ on this CoreELEC box. At every boot it waits up to 60s for a 192.168.x.x LAN IP (ignoring WireGuard/OpenVPN/PPP tunnel interfaces); if none appears, it restarts connman and keeps retrying every 30s for as long as it takes - it only stops once a real LAN IP is actually present. Fixes boots where the network never comes up on its own, including ones where a single connman restart isn't enough. Idempotent - running it again just confirms the files are already installed and the service enabled. Not a Kodi/skin fix - a system-level boot reliability fix, same delivery mechanism (a one-time Program add-on) as the other patches in this repo.
extension.news: 1.3.0: fixed a real-world failure - watchdog used to give up after a single connman restart attempt (60s wait + one restart + 20s check), so if the network took longer than that to recover (e.g. the remote site's router itself was still coming back up), the box was stuck on a bad IP for the rest of that boot with no further retries. Now it keeps restarting connman every 30s indefinitely until a real 192.168.x.x LAN IP is actually present - never gives up, but also never restarts once the IP is good. 1.2.0: now also runs a one-time check at Kodi boot (added the xbmc.service extension point) instead of only ever running when the user manually opens it from Program add-ons - offers the same install confirmation automatically once per box, and if accepted, immediately offers to reboot the whole box right then (a systemd service, not a Kodi feature, so a plain Kodi restart isn't enough) instead of just telling the user to do it themselves later. Only ever asks once, even on "no". 1.1.1: install confirmation now explicitly says a full SYSTEM restart is needed (not just Kodi) - the previous "runs automatically on the next boot" wording didn't make clear the user needs to actually reboot the box, not just restart Kodi, matching the clearer restart wording every other add-on in this repo already uses. 1.1.0: added a settings screen with explicit Install and "Stop and remove service" actions - Kodi has no uninstall hook for script add-ons (clicking Uninstall in the add-on browser just deletes this add-on's files, it never runs any of our code), so the systemd service and script this addon installs to /storage/.config/ would otherwise keep running forever regardless of whether the Kodi addon itself is still installed. Run "Stop and remove service" BEFORE uninstalling. 1.0.0: initial release - packages the network-watchdog systemd service confirmed working on x96max+.

extension.summary: Real fanart backgrounds for the currently playing music artist
extension.description: Lightweight replacement for Artist Slideshow. Looks up TheAudioDB / fanart.tv / Deezer for the currently playing artist and exposes the result via Window(Visualisation).Property(ArtistSlideshow.Image) - the same convention Artist Slideshow itself uses, already read natively by many skins without needing anything else installed. Runs as a proper Kodi background service (started once at Kodi startup) instead of a re-invoked script, avoiding the stuck/zombie "already running" issue. Aeon Nox 5 users can additionally, optionally, install script.cu.lrclyrics.fixed (which patches Aeon Nox 5 directly for this, formerly a separate script.xderecx.aeonnox5lyricsfix addon, merged in 2026-09-10) for a rotating full-screen background bound to this same property - not required for skins that already read it themselves.
extension.news: 1.8.3: updated the description's mention of the optional Aeon Nox 5 companion - script.xderecx.aeonnox5lyricsfix was merged into script.cu.lrclyrics.fixed on 2026-09-10 and no longer exists as a separate addon. 1.8.2: added a one-time notification the first time this service ever starts, confirming it's running and that (unlike other add-ons in this repo) no Kodi restart is needed - xbmc.service add-ons are started immediately by Kodi's own service manager on install/enable. Nothing previously told the user this addon had actually started at all. 1.8.1: added "(Universal)" to the display name so it's clear at a glance in Kodi's Add-ons browser that this works on any skin. 1.8.0: script.xderecx.aeonnox5lyricsfix is no longer a required dependency - this service was always skin-independent (it just exposes a standard Window property), only the Aeon Nox 5 rotating-background display of it needed that patch, and forcing it as a hard dependency for every skin never made sense. Updated the description to stop implying Aeon Nox 5 is needed. 1.7.1: description clarifies this addon is only tested against Aeon Nox 5. 1.7.0: now declares script.xderecx.aeonnox5lyricsfix as a real add-on dependency (this addon does nothing visible without that skin patch applied), so Kodi installs it automatically alongside this one instead of it being an easy-to-miss separate manual step - it still needs to be run once from Program add-ons to actually patch the skin. 1.6.0: now auto-switches to the visualisation screen (rotating fanart + lyrics) whenever audio playback starts, instead of leaving whichever library/browsing screen was open beforehand - so starting an album from anywhere in Kodi jumps straight to the now-playing view. 1.5.0: fixed fanart appearing permanently frozen on one image whenever CU LRC Lyrics is showing (i.e. most of the time). Root cause: the visible screen during playback is usually the lyrics dialog window, not the plain visualisation window - Kodi only continues to actively redraw the topmost open window, so the visualisation window's own image control (bound to our rotating property) stopped getting refreshed the moment the lyrics dialog opened, freezing on whichever image was showing at that instant, even though the underlying property kept updating correctly every 12s. Also tried routing updates through Kodi's native library fanart field via AudioLibrary.SetArtistDetails, but Player.Art(fanart) turned out to be a one-time snapshot per track (not live), so that alone doesn't fix mid-song rotation either - kept it anyway since a real per-track native fanart is still a nice side benefit and survives library rescans reasonably (re-asserted every rotation cycle). The actual fix (paired with a companion aeon-nox-5 skin patch, see skin-overrides/) adds a background image control directly inside the lyrics dialog's own XML, bound to the same rotating property, so it refreshes as part of that window's own active render loop instead of relying on the frozen window underneath. 1.4.0: fixed the artist fanart rotation permanently freezing on one image - Rotator.run() had no exception handling, so any single unhandled error (e.g. a stale path from a race with a fresh download) silently killed the rotation thread for the rest of the Kodi session. Now logs and keeps looping instead. 1.3.0: fixed addon settings showing values with no labels at all (blank rows) - the settings.xml used inline text for each setting's label instead of a numbered string ID resolved via strings.po, which this Kodi build silently fails to render for addon settings. Added a proper resources/language/resource.language.en_gb/strings.po and pointed each setting's label at its string ID, matching how the other working addons in this repo do it. 1.2.0: fixed a real bug - xbmc.Player().getPlayingFile() returns a musicdb://songs/... virtual URL (not a real path) when a track is played from the Kodi music library view, which silently broke library-folder saving (it always fell back to the private cache instead). Now resolves the real on-disk path via Player.GetItem's "file" property first. 1.1.0: added Deezer as a third image source (no API key needed) - mainly helps Slovak/Czech and other regional artists that TheAudioDB/fanart.tv don't have at all. Added an on-screen "searching for fanart..." notification on first fetch for a new artist, so it's clear something is happening during the initial download delay. 1.0.0: initial release.
